title: Insights into Nanoparticles Formation Achieved by Powder Metallurgy Processing Routes of Zn-Mg-(Ag) Alloys for Bioresorbable Implants
content: Bioresorbable implants consisting of Iron (Fe), Magnesium (Mg) and Zinc (Zn)-based materials have garnered considerable interest for the ability to minimize severe long-term effects of non-inert conventional metallic implants [1]. However, the low mechanical properties of the Zn-based materials is a critical limitation for their applications. [1, 2]. As such, several studies have attempted to optimize the mechanical properties of these alloys. For the Zn-Mg alloys, yield strength increase is observed due to the presence of precipitates within the matrix and at grain boundaries [3-8]. Microalloying with e.g. Ag in Zn-rich binary Zn-Mg-(Ag) alloy exhibit an antibacterial effect and strength increase compared to pure Zn [9]; however, the effect of Mg and Ag on the mechanical properties are unclear. In addition, their precipitation states remain unknown and can have deleterious impacts on biodegradation if uncontrolled. Significant characterization efforts of the Mg and Ag distribution is critical to unlock the potential of Zn-based bioresorbable medical devices and implants.
